formation.title: Up Ewig Ungedeelt
formation.text:
The duchies of Schleswig and Holstein are united at last. For centuries these lands have been pulled between Denmark and the Empire, their dukes serving two masters, their people speaking two languages. The Treaty of Ribe declared these lands 'forever undivided', but unity of territory is not yet unity of purpose.

The Holsatian nobles demand a strong duke who can resist Danish encroachment and stand as sovereign in the Empire. But the merchants of Kiel and the farmers of the marshes see a different future: one where the duchy's position between two seas and two civilizations becomes its greatest asset, not a source of weakness.

Shall Schleswig-Holstein forge itself into a single, sovereign state? Or shall it embrace the borderland, becoming the indispensable bridge between Scandinavia and Germany?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We are forever undivided, under one sovereign

modifiers.name: Up Ewig Ungedeelt
modifiers.text: The duchies of Schleswig and Holstein are forever undivided. Under a single sovereign will, the borderland has become a unified state, its governance firm and its borders secure.

options.text: We are the bridge between two worlds

modifiers.name: The Eider Frontier
modifiers.text: Schleswig-Holstein embraces its nature as a bridge between worlds. Danish and German, North Sea and Baltic, Scandinavia and the Empire: all meet and mingle in these duchies, and from this mingling comes prosperity.

advances.name: Deichbau
advances.text: Since the 11th century, the people of the North Sea marshes have built dikes to reclaim land from the sea, creating the rich farmland that sustains Holstein's population.

advances.name: Borderland Governance
advances.text: Holstein's unique position as both a Danish dependency and an Imperial county has bred a tradition of diplomatic flexibility and tolerance of difference.

advances.name: Holsatian Ritterschaft
advances.text: The Holsatian knightly class, serving both Danish and Imperial lords, forms the backbone of the duchy's military and administrative capacity.

advances.name: North Sea Salt
advances.text: The Frisians burn salt peat cut from the tidal flats, and the brine springs of Oldesloe are boiled down in pans. Salt is a vital commodity that preserves fish and meat for trade across northern Europe.

advances.name: The Ochsenweg
advances.text: The great ox road stretches from the pastures of Jutland south to Hamburg and beyond. Vast herds of cattle are driven along this ancient route, enriching every settlement along the way.

advances.name: Treaty of Ribe
advances.text: The 1460 Treaty of Ribe declared Schleswig and Holstein 'forever undivided,' establishing the constitutional foundation that binds the duchies together.

event.title: The Treaty of Ribe
event.text:
On 2 March 1460, in the ancient city of Ribe, the Holsatian nobles elected King Christian I of Denmark as their new count, succeeding the extinct Schauenburg dynasty. In return, Christian swore an oath that would echo through centuries: the duchies of Schleswig and Holstein should remain 'up ewig ungedeelt' (forever undivided).

This simple phrase in Low German became the constitutional foundation of the duchies. But its meaning was contested from the start. Did it mean the duchies were bound together as one state under ducal authority? Or did it mean the estates (the knights and towns who extracted this promise) held a permanent right to share in governance?

The answer will shape the duchy's character for generations.

options.text: The duke rules undivided lands with undivided authority

modifiers.name: Treaty Sovereignty
modifiers.text: The Treaty of Ribe has been interpreted as a mandate for ducal sovereignty, concentrating power in the duke's hands rather than the estates.

options.text: The estates share in the governance of these lands

modifiers.name: Estates Partnership
modifiers.text: The Treaty of Ribe has established a partnership between the duke and the Holstein estates, with merchant towns gaining a voice in governance.

advances.name: Kiel Harbor
advances.text: Kiel's natural harbor on the Baltic gives the duchy a maritime presence, with shipbuilding and trade connecting Holstein to the wider Hanseatic world.

advances.name: Gottorp Court
advances.text: The ducal court at Gottorp Castle, near the old city of Schleswig, is a center of culture and administration, where the duke presides over both Danish and German affairs.

advances.name: Hemmingstedt
advances.text: The disastrous battle of 1500, where Dithmarscher peasants destroyed a ducal army on flooded marshland, taught Schleswig-Holstein the lethal power of defensive terrain and water management.

event.title: The Disaster at Hemmingstedt
event.text:
On 17 February 1500, King John of Denmark and Duke Frederick marched against the free peasant republic of Dithmarschen with an army of over twelve thousand men, including four thousand Landsknechte and two thousand armored knights. The Dithmarscher peasants, barely six thousand strong, met them on flooded ground near the village of Hemmingstedt.

The peasants had opened the sluice gates of their dikes, flooding the low-lying marshes and funneling the invading army into narrow causeways where their numbers counted for nothing. One-third of all the knights of Schleswig and Holstein perished in the mud. The ducal banner fell. It was the worst military humiliation in the history of the duchies.

But from this disaster comes a hard lesson: in these flat, watery lands, fortification and knowledge of the terrain are worth more than cavalry charges. The marsh itself is a weapon for those who know how to wield it.

options.text: We shall never again underestimate the marsh

advances.name: Salt Road Trade
advances.text: Holstein controls sections of the salt road connecting the Luneburg salt mines to the Baltic ports, profiting from the flow of this essential commodity.

advances.name: Dual Sea Shipyards
advances.text: Kiel's shipwrights build vessels suited to both the shallow Baltic and the stormy North Sea, a versatility born of the duchy's unique position between two oceans.

advances.name: Ducal Partition
advances.text: The 1544 partition of Schleswig-Holstein into royal and ducal shares created a complex system of shared governance that, paradoxically, strengthened administrative capacity.

advances.name: Early Reformation
advances.text: Schleswig-Holstein embraced the Lutheran Reformation in 1528, among the earliest territories in Europe to do so, transforming its churches and schools.

advances.name: Gottorp Library
advances.text: The Gottorp dukes assembled a remarkable library and cabinet of curiosities, including the famous Gottorp Globe, a monument to Baroque scientific ambition.

advances.name: Diplomatic Balancing
advances.text: The Holstein-Gottorp dukes mastered the art of playing Denmark against Sweden and both against the Empire, surviving through diplomatic agility rather than military might.

advances.name: Wartime Endurance
advances.text: The Thirty Years' War ravaged the duchies, but the population endured. The survivors rebuilt their farms and towns with a resilience forged in decades of conflict.

advances.name: Eider Canal
advances.text: The canal connecting the Baltic at Kiel to the North Sea via the Eider River transforms Schleswig-Holstein into the maritime crossroads of northern Europe.

event.title: The Eider Canal
event.text:
Since the days of the Vikings, men have dreamed of cutting a channel across the narrow neck of the Jutland peninsula to connect the North Sea to the Baltic. Duke Adolf I of Holstein-Gottorp first proposed the project in 1571, but it took two centuries of engineering advances before construction could begin.

Completed in 1784, the Eider Canal stretches from Kiel on the Baltic to the Eider estuary at Tonning on the North Sea. Ships that once braved weeks of dangerous sailing around the Skagerrak can now transit in days. The canal transforms Schleswig-Holstein from a peripheral borderland into the pivot point of northern European maritime commerce.

Shall the canal serve primarily as a strategic asset for the duchy's naval ambitions, or as a commercial highway enriching its merchant class?

options.text: A strategic waterway for our fleet

modifiers.name: Strategic Waterway
modifiers.text: The Eider Canal serves as a strategic corridor, allowing rapid movement of ships between the North Sea and the Baltic without the dangerous journey around Jutland.

options.text: A highway of commerce for our merchants

modifiers.name: Commercial Corridor
modifiers.text: The Eider Canal has become a commercial artery, enabling goods to flow between the two seas and enriching the towns along its banks.

advances.name: University of Kiel
advances.text: Founded in 1665, the Christiana Albertina at Kiel is the duchy's premier center of learning, training scholars, jurists, and administrators for service across the north.

event.title: Christiana Albertina
event.text:
On 5 October 1665, Duke Christian Albert of Holstein-Gottorp founded a university at Kiel, naming it the Christiana Albertina after himself and his father. The duke endowed the institution with lands and privileges, drawing scholars from across the Protestant north.

The university quickly becomes a center of jurisprudence, theology, and natural philosophy. Its professors train the administrators who will govern the duchies, and its students carry the learning of Kiel to courts and counting houses across northern Europe. In a land torn between Danish and German claims, the university provides a distinctly Holsatian center of intellectual identity.

options.text: May Kiel become a beacon of northern learning

advances.name: Holstein Cattle
advances.text: The black-and-white Holstein-Friesian breed, developed on the rich marshland pastures, becomes renowned across Europe for its prodigious milk production.

advances.name: Gutswirtschaft
advances.text: The reorganization of ducal estates into rationalized agricultural operations increases yields and tax revenues, driving rural modernization.

advances.name: National Movement
advances.text: The Schleswig-Holstein movement revives the Treaty of Ribe's promise, demanding that the duchies remain united and free from Danish absorption.

advances.name: Kiel Revolution
advances.text: Revolutionary fervor sweeps through Kiel's workers and sailors, demanding constitutional rights and political representation.

advances.name: Industrial Shipyards
advances.text: Kiel's shipyards industrialize, adopting iron and steam construction to produce warships that will anchor a modern navy.

advances.name: Border Resolution
advances.text: The Schleswig-Holstein wars settle the centuries-old border question through force of arms, establishing a clear frontier between Danish and German sovereignty.

destiny.name: Destiny of the Duchies
destiny.text: Schleswig-Holstein has been forged into a single state. Now the duchy must decide its future course: whether to pursue sovereign power or commercial preeminence.

event.title: Destiny of the Duchies
event.text:
The union of Schleswig and Holstein is complete, but the true work has only begun. These marshlands and harbors, these cattle roads and salt pans: they are the foundation of something greater. The question is what we shall build upon them.

Shall we forge a sovereign state that answers to no Danish king, no Imperial diet? Or shall we embrace our nature as the bridge between worlds, growing rich on the commerce that must pass through our narrow isthmus?

destiny.name: The Schleswig Question
destiny.text: Seize the old duchy of Schleswig from Danish control. Take Flensburg and the city of Schleswig to unite the historic duchies under one sovereign will. Requires an army of at least 30,000 men.

conditions.text: Chose the Up Ewig Ungedeelt destiny
Own Flensburg, or a subject owns it
Own Slesvig, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Schleswig Question
event.text:
Flensburg and the old city of Schleswig are ours. For centuries, these lands were held by the Danish crown, their German-speaking population subject to a foreign sovereign. No more. The duchy of Schleswig is reunited with Holstein under a single ruler.

The Danish king will not accept this quietly. But the lesson of the Treaty of Ribe still holds: these lands are forever undivided, and now they are forever ours.

destiny.name: Masters of the Elbe
destiny.text: Extend the duchy's reach to the great port of Hamburg and secure South Jutland. The Elbe estuary is the gateway to northern Germany and must answer to Holstein. Requires an army of 50,000 and international standing.

conditions.text: Own Hamburg, or a subject owns it
Own Aabenraa, or a subject owns it

event.title: Masters of the Elbe
event.text:
Hamburg, the great free city of the Elbe, and the towns of South Jutland now fall within our sphere. The duchy commands the lower Elbe: the artery through which half of northern Germany's trade must flow.

This expansion demands a choice. Shall we impose iron discipline on our new territories, crushing resistance and forging a unified military state? Or shall we grant charters and privileges, incorporating Hamburg's merchant tradition and Jutland's communities as willing partners?

options.text: Iron discipline shall bind these lands

modifiers.name: Iron Discipline
modifiers.text: The new territories are held by military force. Garrisons enforce order and separatist sentiment is crushed, but the duchy's prestige suffers from its heavy-handed methods.

options.text: Grant charters and earn their loyalty

modifiers.name: Elbe Charters
modifiers.text: New subjects receive charters guaranteeing their traditional rights. They serve the duchy willingly, though maintaining such a diverse realm requires a larger military budget.

destiny.name: The Sovereign Duchy
destiny.text: Take Copenhagen itself and the ancient treaty-city of Ribe, ending Danish pretensions over the duchies forever. Requires a powerful army of 75,000, a full treasury, and a prestigious reputation.

conditions.text: Own Copenhagen, or a subject owns it
Own Ribe, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Sovereign Duchy
event.text:
Copenhagen has fallen. The ancient seat of Danish power, the city that claimed suzerainty over our duchies for centuries, is now subject to our will. With Ribe (the very city where the treaty of eternal unity was sworn) also in our hands, the circle is complete.

Schleswig-Holstein is no longer a borderland caught between greater powers. It is a sovereign state in its own right, master of both shores of the Eider, both banks of the Elbe, and now the Sound itself.

Shall we use this power for further conquest, imposing our will across the north? Or shall we build a federation of northern states, leading through diplomacy rather than force?

options.text: We shall impose our sovereign will

modifiers.name: Sovereign's Will
modifiers.text: The duchy's intelligence network extends across the north, and war comes cheaply to a sovereign who has proven his strength by taking Copenhagen.

options.text: We shall lead a federation of equals

modifiers.name: Northern Federation
modifiers.text: The duchy leads a coalition of northern states through diplomatic weight and constitutional authority, integrating new members into a growing federation.

destiny.name: The Salt Bridge
destiny.text: Build a commercial bridge between the two seas. Grow Kiel, whose Umschlag fair is where the nobles of the duchies borrow and settle their debts, and ensure salt flows through the duchy's markets. Requires 1,000 gold in the treasury.

conditions.text: We own Kiel and its development is at least 31

children.text: Salt is produced in the market
Salt is traded in the market

event.title: The Salt Bridge
event.text:
Kiel's Umschlag has become the money market of the duchies, and salt (the white gold of the north) flows through our markets in abundance. The foundations of a great commercial state are laid.

Every barrel of herring preserved with our salt, every hide cured with our brine, every road and canal that carries these goods: all enrich the duchy's counting houses. Schleswig-Holstein is becoming what its geography always intended: a bridge of commerce between two worlds.

options.text: The bridge is built on salt and silver

destiny.name: Between Two Seas
destiny.text: Seize Bremen to control the Weser trade and develop cloth manufacturing in the capital market. The duchy must become the textile crossroads of the north. Requires 2,000 gold and international prestige.

conditions.text: Own Bremen, or a subject owns it

children.text: Cloth is produced in the market
Cloth is traded in the market

event.title: Between Two Seas
event.text:
Bremen is ours, and cloth from our looms reaches markets on both seas. The duchy now controls the transit routes between the North Sea and the Baltic, with manufacturing capacity to add value to the raw goods that pass through.

Shall we exploit this position through strict monopoly, controlling prices and excluding competitors? Or shall we declare open ports, attracting traders from every nation with the promise of low tariffs and safe harbors?

modifiers.name: Transit Monopoly
modifiers.text: Strict control of the two-seas transit route enriches the duchy's naval forces and banking houses, though protectionism draws suspicion from trading partners.

options.text: Open ports shall draw all comers

modifiers.name: Open Ports
modifiers.text: Free ports attract merchants from every nation, reducing naval costs through shared patrolling and keeping the seas safe for all.

destiny.name: The Northern Nexus
destiny.text: Own Bruges and Bergen, the anchors of the North Sea and Atlantic trade, and build Merchants Quarters in three of the duchy's harbors. Schleswig-Holstein shall become the warehouse of Europe. Requires 3,000 gold and high prestige.

conditions.text: Own Bruges, or a subject owns it
Own Bergen, or a subject owns it
At least 3 of our ports have Merchants Quarters or a later trade building that replaced them

event.title: The Northern Nexus
event.text:
From Bergen's cod wharves to the cloth halls of Bruges, from the salt pans of Holstein to the spice warehouses of the Sound: all roads of northern commerce now pass through Schleswig-Holstein. The duchy has become what the old Hanse once dreamed of: the nexus of northern trade, the warehouse of Europe.

Shall we cement this position as a great entrepot, a neutral ground where all nations trade? Or shall we revive the spirit of the Hanseatic League, building a formal coalition of trading cities under our leadership?

options.text: We are the entrepot of the north

modifiers.name: Northern Entrepot
modifiers.text: The duchy serves as a neutral warehouse for all of northern Europe, building naval prestige and stabilizing the economy while the army's needs take second priority.

options.text: We shall lead a new Hanseatic League

modifiers.name: New Hanseatic League
modifiers.text: A revived Hanseatic League under Schleswig-Holstein's leadership projects commercial power across the seas, with member cities contributing to shared naval defense.

units.name: Holsatian Marschbauer
units.text: Peasant militia from the North Sea marshes, hardened by lifetimes of fighting the sea itself. They know every dike, every sluice gate, every patch of treacherous ground.

units.name: Holstein Ochsentreiber
units.text: Mounted cattle drovers who guide vast herds along the Ochsenweg. Excellent scouts and skirmishers, they know every ford and pasture from Jutland to Hamburg.

units.name: Kiel Pinass
units.text: A fast patrol vessel from the Kiel shipyards, built shallow-drafted for the Baltic but sturdy enough for the North Sea. Ideal for anti-piracy patrols and coastal trade escort.

buildings.name: Deichamt
buildings.text: A dike authority office coordinating the construction and maintenance of sea defenses, the drainage of marshland, and the management of reclaimed farmland.

buildings.name: Saline
buildings.text: A salt works on salt land: brine drawn from the springs and boiled down in iron pans, as at Oldesloe in Stormarn, where the duchies boiled salt from the twelfth century on. The salt that preserves the fish and meat of northern Europe comes out of it in greater measure.

where.text: The location's raw material is Salt

buildings.name: Hafenkontor
buildings.text: A merchant counting house at Kiel harbor, managing the flow of goods between the North Sea and Baltic trading networks.

buildings.name: Ochsenweg Station
buildings.text: A trading station along the great ox road where cattle are rested, weighed, taxed, and traded. Leather workers process hides alongside the pens.

buildings.name: Warft
buildings.text: An artificial dwelling mound raised above the flood line, protecting settlements from North Sea storm surges. The Halligen islanders have built these since the Middle Ages.

buildings.name: Kieler Werft
buildings.text: A shipyard on the Kiel Fjord, building vessels suited to both the shallow Baltic and the open North Sea, a versatility unique to this dual-coast duchy.

buildings.name: Lutherkirche
buildings.text: A reformed parish church established after the 1528 Reformation, serving as a center of Lutheran preaching, education, and community governance.

buildings.name: Gutshof
buildings.text: A rationalized ducal estate applying Enlightenment principles to agriculture, with improved crop rotation, drainage, and estate management.

buildings.name: Christiana Albertina
buildings.text: The university founded by Duke Christian Albert in 1665, a center of Protestant scholarship, jurisprudence, and natural philosophy in the heart of Holstein.

buildings.name: Turnhalle
buildings.text: A gymnastic hall that doubles as a meeting place for the national movement, where political rallies and civic education stoke the fire of Schleswig-Holstein unity.

buildings.name: Kieler Schloss
buildings.text: The sovereign palace at Kiel, seat of the independent duchy's court and government. A fortress-residence commanding the Baltic shore, symbolizing Holstein's triumph over Danish suzerainty.

buildings.name: Zweiuferkontor
buildings.text: The Two-Shore Counting House, a grand mercantile exchange managing the transit trade between the North Sea and the Baltic. Agents of every northern trading nation maintain offices here.

list.name: Schleswig-Holsteinische Ritterschaft
list.text: Constituted by the Treaty of Ribe in 1460, the united knighthood of both duchies sat as a single corporate body of Equites Originarii at Bordesholm. Its great Junker estates (Rantzau, Reventlow, Ahlefeldt, Brockdorff) covered most of eastern Holstein and were exempt from ducal taxation. The Ritterschaft was the constitutional defender of the up-ewig-ungedeelt principle: properly cultivated it musters the heavy cavalry of the realm and binds the duke to his oath; neglected it calcifies into a hereditary brake on every reform, and Holstein peasants on the adelige Güter sink into Leibeigenschaft.

list.name: Landtag der Stände
list.text: The tripartite estates assembly of the duchies, established alongside the union of 1460. Three benches sat: the Ritterschaft, the cathedral chapters of Schleswig and Lübeck, and the Vier Städte (Schleswig, Flensburg, Kiel, Rendsburg). The Landtag voted Bede taxes, registered ducal Verordnungen, and arbitrated between the Glückstadt and Gottorp lines after the 1544 partition. When properly convened at Kiel and Rendsburg, it lent legitimacy to royal edicts; when bypassed, the three benches retaliated by stalling legislation and withdrawing the duchies' burgher confidence.

list.name: Kieler Umschlag
list.text: The annual financial fair held at Kiel in the week after Epiphany. First documented in a 1469 letter from the Lübeck council, by the 16th and 17th centuries it had become the principal credit market of northern Germany, the duchies, and the Kingdom of Denmark. Holstein Junkers lent at six to seven percent to Danish kings, Hanseatic merchants, and military entrepreneurs; most of the realm's sovereign debt was rolled over each January at Kiel. Maintained, it cheapens crown borrowing and thickens the burgher purse; neglected, rates climb and Holstein freeholds fall into the hands of foreclosing creditors: the late-16th-century pattern of Bauernlegen.

list.name: Adelige Klöster
list.text: The four Protestant noble convents (Itzehoe, Preetz, Uetersen, and St. Johannis at Schleswig) that survived the Reformation as collegiate foundations for unmarried daughters of the Schleswig-Holstein nobility. Reorganised by the Klosterordnung after 1542, they retained vast church-estate lands, were governed by elected Pröpstinnen drawn from the Ritterschaft, and served as both noble retirement-houses and a Lutheran-aristocratic learned milieu. Sustained, they anchor a literate clerical-noble culture; decayed, they devolve into rent-extracting absentee landlords whose tax-free estates the burgher towns increasingly resent.

list.name: Deutsche Kanzlei
list.text: The German Chancery: the duchies' core administrative organ, conducting all business in German in pointed contrast to Copenhagen's Danske Kancelli. Based at Gottorp under the Holstein-Gottorp dukes with a counterpart at Glückstadt for the royal share after 1648, it codified the Schleswigsches Landrecht and the Holsteinisches Landrecht and dispatched the Verordnungen that governed them. From 1806 it was consolidated as the Schleswig-Holstein-Lauenburg Kanzlei. Properly staffed by Kanzleiräte trained at Kiel and Helmstedt, it integrates the patchwork of Amter, Klöster, and Adelsguter into a coherent state; underfunded, it devolves into a paper-shuffling sinecure ignored in the marshes.
